From: Sarah Langston <sarah@mediform.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway concern — PO in procurement queue

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the team was impressed with the latency numbers on the smaller models. Two quick updates from our side: procurement has started vendor onboarding but our finance team routed the PO for a security checklist and vendor risk review. That process typically adds 7–10 business days for us.

We're worried the pilot environment will expire before the PO clears. Is there any way Redwood can "pause" the countdown or grant a short buffer while the PO circulates? We want to keep the demo live for the engineering team so momentum doesn't stall.

I can share the PO draft and procurement ticket if that helps. Expected PO issuance date (optimistic): Aug 4.

Thanks,
Sarah Langston
Director of Engineering, Mediform Health
procurement@mediform.com

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the heads-up and for sharing the PO draft. Totally understand the need to keep the eval live while procurement runs the gauntlet.

Short answer: yes, we can do a temporary hold on the trial countdown. I need to confirm internally one exception — finance approval for a 7-day keepalive voucher. I copied Marissa (AE) and Priyom (SE) to expedite.

If agreeable, our proposal:
- Freeze the pilot timer for up to 7 calendar days starting when we confirm (we can backdate to today if needed).
- If PO clears earlier we’ll resume normal billing/use and reconcile any prorated credits.
- We’ll need either the PO draft or a note from procurement with the expected clearance date for audit.

I’ve attached the draft terms we use for short keepalive grants so legal/finance can see the shape of it. If that looks fine to your procurement team, we’ll push approval on our side.

Next steps for us: Marissa will confirm commercial approval; Priyom will note the account change so the sandbox access persists.

Talk soon,

- Requirements on your side: keep the PO draft on the procurement ticket or send a short note from procurement with the expected clearance date (Aug 4). This is for our audit and to avoid repeated concessions.
- If the PO clears before Aug 7 we’ll reconcile usage and resume normal terms immediately.
